Substrate (bootstrap/src/emit/main.wat):

      LPVar (360)    — direct binding
      LPCon (363)    — recurse args list

    single-expr case (LMatch encountered via LLet-value descent).

mentl/a0beab7:
Effect-op surface in the wheel ends each op with the resume-discipline
annotation `@resume=OneShot` (or MultiShot / Either) on the same
source line as the op's signature. The seed's $parse_effect_ops loop
calls $skip_sep after each op's ret-ty parse, but $skip_sep advances
only through TNewline + TSemicolon, leaving the parser positioned at
TAt. Subsequent loop iterations consumed `@`, `resume`, `=`, then
mistook `OneShot` (TIdent) as the next op-name, mangling registration
and dropping the actual subsequent ops.

Result on the wheel: load_i32 + first op of each effect registered;
load_i8 + store_i8 + mem_copy + i32_xor (later ops in the same effect)
silently dropped. ~70 missing-variable diagnostics per file.

Fix: $skip_annotation_to_eol — when pos is at TAt, scan forward to
the next newline / TEof / TRBrace, leaving the EOL for $skip_sep.
The seed first-light surface drops the discipline; the named
follow-up Hβ.first-light.effect-op-resume-discipline-substrate
encodes the discipline into the op's TFun row.

Verified on lib/runtime/memory.nx + lib/runtime/strings.nx: load_i8 /
store_i8 / mem_copy no longer surface as E_MissingVariable.

stoop/a0da89a:
A photograph was screened to two tones once, on intake, and the result was
final: a dark phone photo dithered to mud and the only fix was the camera
file. The device now keeps a small greyscale original beside each
photograph, and a photo cutting or a page's own photograph can be made
lighter or darker, or screened as halftone dots or hard copier contrast
instead of grain. Each new screening is a new photograph with its own id,
so an issue on the shelf keeps the one it was printed with, and asking for
the same settings twice gives back the one already made. The originals
live in two side stores of the photo database, are swept with the last
photograph made from them, and never ride in a file. A photograph that
came in somebody's file has no original here and offers no controls.
